title: Algebraic Bertini lemma for a generic linear combination
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension], meaning that finitely many elements generate $K$ as a field over $k$. Suppose $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $n\geq1$, $g_1,\ldots,g_n\in K$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be indeterminates. Put $\Omega=\operatorname{Frac}(K[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$, the field of fractions of the polynomial domain [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Assume there exist $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in k$ such that the ordered family $x_1,\ldots,x_n,\sum_{i=1}^n g_ix_i,\sum_{i=1}^n c_ig_i$ in $\Omega$ is algebraically independent over $k$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is geometrically irreducible over the subfield $k(x_1,\ldots,x_n,\sum_{i=1}^n g_ix_i)$ generated by these indicated elements.

proof.text: Write $\xi=\sum_i g_i x_i$ and $\delta=\sum_i c_i g_i$. For each $a\in k$, the substitution $\sigma_a(x_i)=x_i+a c_i$ and $\sigma_a|_K=\mathrm{id}$ defines an automorphism of $\Omega$; it sends $\xi$ to $\xi+a\delta$ and fixes $\delta$. Put $K_0=k(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, $K_1=K_0(\xi)$, and $K_2=K_0(\xi,\delta)$. Then $\sigma_a$ preserves $K_0$ and $K_2$, and $K_2/K_0$ is purely transcendental of degree two by the assumed algebraic independence.

By the geometric-irreducibility criterion [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-separable], it is enough to prove that every element $\theta\in\Omega$ separably algebraic over $K_1$ lies in $K_1$. Fix such a $\theta$.

Let $K'_2$ be the subfield of elements of $\Omega$ separably algebraic over $K_2$. The extension $\Omega/K_2$ is finitely generated, so [lem-zl-finite-separable-closure] gives that $K'_2/K_2$ is finite. It is separable by construction. Hence [lem-zl-finite-intermediate-fields] gives only finitely many intermediate fields between $K_2$ and $K'_2$.

Assume first that $k$ is infinite. The infinitely many fields $K_2(\sigma_a(\theta))$ therefore include two equal ones; choose distinct $a_1,a_2\in k$ with this equality. Set $\theta_i=\sigma_{a_i}(\theta)$ and $\xi_i=\sigma_{a_i}(\xi)=\xi+a_i\delta$. Solving the two linear equations gives $K_2=K_0(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ and $\xi_1,\xi_2$ are algebraically independent over $K_0$. Since $\theta_1$ is algebraic over $K_0(\xi_1)$, $\xi_2$ is transcendental over $K_0(\xi_1,\theta_1)$.

The extension $\Omega/K_0$ is geometrically irreducible by [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-transcendental], applied to the geometrically irreducible extension $K/k$ and the variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. Its subextension $K_0(\xi_1,\theta_1)/K_0$ is geometrically irreducible by [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-subextension]. Applying [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-add-transcendental] with the transcendental element $\xi_2$ gives that $K_0(\xi_1,\xi_2,\theta_1)/K_0(\xi_2)$ is geometrically irreducible.

By the choice of $a_1,a_2$, the field $K_0(\xi_1,\xi_2,\theta_1)$ equals $K_2(\theta_1)=K_2(\theta_2)=K_0(\xi_1,\xi_2,\theta_2)$. The element $\theta_2$ is separably algebraic over $K_0(\xi_2)$, so the converse direction of [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-separable] applied to the preceding geometrically irreducible extension gives $\theta_2\in K_0(\xi_2)$. Applying $\sigma_{a_2}^{-1}$ yields $\theta\in K_0(\xi)=K_1$.

Now suppose that $k$ is finite. Introduce a new indeterminate $t$. By [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-transcendental], $K(t)/k(t)$ is geometrically irreducible. The elements $x_1,\ldots,x_n,\xi,\delta$ remain algebraically independent over $k(t)$, since clearing a denominator in a polynomial relation over $k(t)$ would give a relation over $k$ after comparing coefficients of the independent variable $t$.

The infinite-field argument in Steps 2--6, applied with base field $k(t)$ and extension $K(t)$, proves that $K(t,x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ is geometrically irreducible over $k(t,x_1,\ldots,x_n,\xi)$. Every hypothesis used there is preserved: $K(t)/k(t)$ is finitely generated, $k(t)$ is infinite, and the displayed algebraic independence was just checked.

Finally, apply the converse direction of [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-transcendental] to the transcendental extension obtained by adjoining $t$ to $\Omega/k(x_1,\ldots,x_n,\xi)$. This descends geometric irreducibility from $K(t,x_1,\ldots,x_n)/k(t,x_1,\ldots,x_n,\xi)$ to the required $\Omega/k(x_1,\ldots,x_n,\xi)$.
